name: poll_flags_with_countdown_callback
description: Loops on a status routine, toggling the low bit of a flag byte in the object record. When the second flag bit is set it runs a 25-tick countdown that calls a stored callback, then clears the second flag bit and resets two long fields before polling again.

name: service_status_flag_loop
description: Polls a status routine while the second flag bit is clear, clearing a field on each pass. Once that bit is set it runs the 25-tick callback countdown, clears the second flag bit, resets two long fields, and returns to the polling loop.

name: run_countdown_then_poll
description: Runs a 25-tick countdown that invokes a stored callback until the counter reaches zero. It then clears the second flag bit, resets two long fields in the object record, and loops polling a status routine while toggling the low flag bit.

name: finish_countdown_then_poll
description: Clears a field, calls a routine, and decrements a countdown that invokes a stored callback while it stays nonzero. On completion it clears the second flag bit, resets two long fields, and enters the same status polling loop.

name: clear_flag_and_poll_countdown
description: Clears the second flag bit, resets two long fields, and polls a status routine until the second flag bit is set. It then arms a 25-tick countdown with a stored callback and a large negative offset value, and returns to polling.

name: reset_channel_register_sequence
description: Clears the low flag bit and toggles bit seven of a control word in the record. It then writes four to a 16-bit field several times with calls between, setting bit four of the control word partway through, and zeroes the control word at the end.

name: toggle_control_word_and_write
description: Toggles bit seven of a control word, writes four to a 16-bit field, then sets bit four and writes four to that field again several times. It zeroes the control word at the end, without first clearing the low flag bit.

name: write_five_byte_pixel_span
description: Computes a byte address from an x and y coordinate pair, shifted and offset, using a row stride stored in the record. It writes four copies of one byte followed by a fifth byte with a different value at that address.

name: loop_toggle_flag_on_compare
description: Sets a 16-bit field to 225 and copies a word into another field. It then loops forever, setting bit four of the control word and clearing it again whenever a compared state differs from 32, zeroing a field and calling a routine each pass.

name: dispatch_jump_table_entry
description: Stores a constant in a field of the object record, then jumps through a table indexed by a word from the record. The decompiler could not recover the table targets, so the individual handlers are unknown.

name: initialize_record_then_scan
description: Advances a 16-bit coordinate field by four, sets several record fields and a flag bit, and reads a table value by a counter index. It then runs scan loops that read values from a routine until a sentinel of two is returned.

name: copy_record_fields_conditionally
description: When a status bit is clear, it reads a sequence of small values through a routine. If the checks on those values pass, it copies two 32-bit fields from the input record into the destination record.

name: initialize_object_record_defaults
description: Initializes a set of fields in an object record, including two 32-bit values, a flag bit, and a command word. It then sets a parameter word and an enabled word in a second record and clears the control word.

name: adjust_counter_from_input_pair
description: Sets a status bit, and when an enable bit is active it reads input values through a routine. A match on the first pair steps a 16-bit counter up by two, a match on the second pair steps it down by two, and either match clears the status bit.

name: adjust_counter_from_directional_input
description: When an enable bit is set and a second flag is clear, it reads directional-style input values through a routine and steps a 16-bit counter by two in one direction or the other. Some reads apply a temporary offset of eight around the update.

name: relay_calls_to_three_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists for this 105-instruction routine and its exact behaviour is unknown. It is called by three routines and calls an empty stub and three further unnamed routines.

name: configure_object_and_invoke_setup
description: Writes several 16-bit configuration fields to the object record, including limits, a size and a callback pointer. It sets a step count of one, calls a routine, and then clears the record's flag word.

name: clear_first_long_field
description: Writes zero to the 32-bit value at the record pointer and returns. The facts list a short text reference, but the pseudo-code shows only this clear, so any role for that text is unknown.

name: relay_calls_to_two_routines
description: The decompiler timed out on this 11-instruction routine, so its body is unknown from the pseudo-code. It is reached through an address-taken reference from two routines and calls two unnamed routines.

name: chain_two_routine_calls
description: The decompiler timed out on this 25-instruction routine, so its body is unknown from the pseudo-code. It is reached through an address-taken reference from two routines and calls two unnamed routines.

name: dispatch_two_unnamed_calls
description: The decompiler timed out on this 13-instruction routine, so its body is unknown from pseudo-code. It is reached through an address-taken reference from two routines and calls two unnamed routines.

name: sequence_two_unnamed_calls
description: The decompiler timed out on this 8-instruction routine, so its body is unknown from pseudo-code. It is reached through an address-taken reference from two routines and calls two unnamed routines.

name: advance_wrapping_counter_on_flag
description: When bit six of a status byte in one record is clear, it clears bit one of a flag byte in the second record. Otherwise, if bit one is still clear, it sets it, increments a counter in the base record, and wraps the counter to zero once it exceeds three.

name: start_audio_channel_dma
description: Writes location and length registers for audio channels zero and one, then writes the DMA control register with the enable bit set. The decompiler timed out, so the exact register values are not recovered.

key: Alien 3 (1992)(Virgin)[cr PDY][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf bytes 14336-14848 (code never loaded by a reference run):0:0000
name: copy_word_when_state_matches
description: Tests a condition flag and two values reached through the input pointer. When both values match their expected states, it copies a word from a fixed offset in the input record into a global variable.

name: invoke_boot_library_routine
description: Boot-block entry that calls one routine and one Exec library function. The decompiled body is partly unreliable because the decompiler flagged bad instruction data, so only the call structure is described.

name: issue_two_io_requests
description: Makes two Exec I/O requests, filling a request block for each with a command value of two and its own length, offset and transfer fields. It then transfers control to a fixed routine.

name: return_two_register_values
description: Makes two unnamed calls and then returns the contents of two data registers as one combined 64-bit value. The callees are not identified from the facts.

key: Hunter (1991)(Activision)[cr FLT][t D-Tect].adf boot-block load +$14A00 to $030000 (5632 bytes):0:0020
name: process_hunk_load_records
description: Compares each record type read from the loader stream against AmigaDOS hunk type codes to choose executable loading or relocation steps. It also writes to a 16-colour palette register, and the decompiler flagged bad instruction data, so details are partial.

name: extract_shifted_bit_value
description: Reads a longword from the address register at a small negative offset and writes its low byte into the low half of a destination word. It returns the longword shifted right by one place with the top bit forced on.

key: Hunter (1991)(Activision)[cr FLT][t D-Tect].adf boot-block load +$14A00 to $030000 (5632 bytes):0:0130
name: shift_register_bits_with_refill
description: Shifts a data register right one bit per pass for a count taken from another register. It calls a routine to refill the register whenever it becomes zero, and the loop runs once per count.

name: extract_shifted_bit_value
description: Reads a longword from the address register at a small negative offset and writes its low byte into the low half of a destination word. It returns the longword shifted right by one place with the top bit forced on.

key: Hunter (1991)(Activision)[cr FLT][t D-Tect].adf boot-block load +$400 to $020000 (16384 bytes):0:0130
name: shift_register_bits_with_refill
description: Shifts a data register right one bit per pass for a count taken from another register. It calls a routine to refill the register whenever it becomes zero, and the loop runs once per count.

name: load_table_entry_fields
description: Multiplies an index by 22 to find an entry in a fixed table. It copies the entry's first word, plus one, into one record field, and copies four further words into four other record fields.

name: copy_record_fields_into_slots
description: Calls three routines, then copies six 16-bit values from one record into two groups of fields in a second record. One of the copied values is shifted left by three bits.

name: call_routine_with_flag_word
description: Stores the maximum positive 16-bit value in a flag word, calls a routine through a pointer held in the record, then writes a different fixed pattern into the same word.

name: store_position_and_offset_fields
description: Stores two input words into record fields, then writes two derived fields made by adding 128 and 44 to those inputs. It then copies two further input values into the record.

name: copy_table_row_into_record
description: Copies ten consecutive words from a table row, selected by one input and scaled by 22, into the record. The destination position is computed from a second input, also scaled by 22.

name: load_indexed_table_block
description: Stores an input index in the record and looks up a block in a fixed table scaled by 46. It copies ten longwords from that block into the record, stores the block pointer, and copies a further run of longwords, making five routine calls in total.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: An empty routine that returns to its caller without doing anything. The facts show a single caller and no other effect.

name: fill_four_strided_longwords
description: Stores a starting longword into four entries spaced eight bytes apart in a buffer, writing its low and high halves into each entry. Each following entry gets the value increased by a fixed step of 2400.

name: fill_strided_longwords_by_step
description: Fills a run of entries in a record-owned buffer with longword values, starting from an input value and adding a step read from the record. The entry count comes from another record field, and the start offset from a third.

name: copy_table_block_into_record
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a block of a global table, selected by an input index scaled by 64, into the record starting at a fixed offset.

name: copy_indexed_block_to_global
description: Stores the global table's base address in a record field, then copies sixteen longwords from a block selected by an input index scaled by 64 back into the start of that table.

name: set_flags_and_return_mask
description: Advances a word in the input record by eight, sets two flag bits in a control word at an indexed position, clears bit five of a status byte and zeroes a longword field. It returns the input value with its low byte forced on.

name: set_flags_and_return_byte
description: Sets two flag bits in a control word at an indexed position, clears bit five of a status byte and zeroes a longword field. It returns the input byte combined with a fixed mask.

name: clear_status_and_return_byte
description: Clears bit five of a status byte, zeroes a longword field, and returns the input byte combined with a fixed mask. The listing shown is shorter than the reported instruction count, so only these visible steps are described.

name: return_absolute_difference_to_target
description: Uses a record word when a status bit is clear and the value fifteen when it is set, subtracts a second record word from it, and returns the absolute value of the result.

name: wait_for_status_bit_clear
description: Zeroes a longword field, makes several calls with a word field temporarily set to fifteen, then waits in a loop until bit five of a status byte is clear.

name: wait_after_temporarily_zeroed_call
description: Temporarily zeroes a word field around a call and restores it, makes another call, then waits in a loop until bit five of a status byte is clear.

name: spin_until_status_clears
description: Loops until bit five of a status byte in the record is clear, then returns. It makes no calls.

name: set_status_flag_from_input
description: When the input value is nonzero it calls a routine and sets bit five of a status byte. When the input is zero it clears bits five and four of that byte instead.

name: store_four_parameter_words
description: Stores the first input into two record fields, the second input into a third field, and a fourth value into a fourth field, then returns.

name: negate_and_reload_parameter
description: Negates one stored word, copies a second stored word into the first field of its pair, and sets bit five of the status byte.

name: step_timed_sequence_counter
description: Decrements a byte counter, and when it wraps negative it reloads from a second byte and counts down a word. When that word reaches zero it clears status flags, and it negates a stored value if a flag bit was set; the routine also makes calls to unnamed routines.

name: scan_offset_within_bounds
description: Moves a stepping offset by one per pass for a count taken from the input, stopping when the value leaves the range zero to fifteen. It then scans a fixed byte table over sixteen steps, calling a routine when a table byte and a status bit are both zero.

name: advance_position_and_call_routine
description: Adds an input value to a record word, then calls a routine sixteen times. It calls the routine again once per step, with the step count taken from a second record word less sixteen, while that count stays nonnegative.

name: add_signed_offset_to_bytes
description: Adds a table byte, read from 192 bytes past the input pointer, into three consecutive bytes. The table byte is negated when the sign input is negative.

name: return_high_nibble_third_byte
description: Reads three consecutive bytes and returns the high nibble of the last one.

name: compute_nibble_differences_into_buffer
description: Writes a run of bytes into a global buffer, each one the high nibble of the difference between a routine code byte and the matching byte in a second buffer. The run length is three times one more than a record field.

name: copy_strided_code_bytes
description: Copies three bytes per pass from a fixed source region into a global buffer. The pass count comes from a record field, plus one.

name: clear_strided_buffer_after_wait
description: Waits until bit five of a status byte is clear, then zeroes three bytes per pass in a global buffer. The pass count comes from a record field plus one, and a word field in the record is zeroed at the end.

name: pack_nibbles_into_two_buffers
description: Writes two bytes from each of two input words, placing the low nibble of each value into the high nibble of an output byte. The results go into two separate output buffers.

name: pack_high_nibbles_from_code
description: Sets a word field to fifteen and stores the low nibble of an input in another field, then makes three calls. It then writes the high nibbles of three-byte groups from a code region into a global buffer, with the count taken from a record field plus one.

name: build_nibble_table_from_list
description: Zeroes a sixteen-entry byte table, calling a routine after each write. It then walks a sentinel-terminated list of words from the record and keeps the entries whose value falls inside a 64-value range. The later steps are not fully shown by the listing.

name: tick_countdown_timers
description: Decrements several 16-bit countdown timers in the record, each gated by a status bit. When a timer goes negative it reloads to fifteen and clears its related status bit, and some expiries call routines.

name: invert_flagged_table_bytes
description: Walks an eight-byte-spaced table from its last entry to its first. Each entry whose byte is nonzero or whose flag bit is set is inverted and a routine is called for it.

name: write_nibble_across_rows
description: Sets a status flag, then writes a source byte to one buffer location. When a second source byte is nonzero it merges a masked nibble into thirteen locations spaced forty bytes apart instead.

name: step_counter_toward_limit
description: When a status bit is set and two other conditions hold, it moves a byte field one step toward zero. It also nudges a word field one step toward thirty-eight, stopping once it reaches that value.

name: write_running_sums_until_end
description: Walks pairs of longwords, writing a running total into the first of each pair and adding the second value into the total. It stops when the second value of a pair is negative.

name: skip_pairs_until_terminator
description: Advances through pairs of longwords until a negative value appears in the second slot, without writing anything. The facts show the routine calls an empty stub.

name: clear_blocks_and_set_marker
description: Clears a run of 32-byte blocks, with the block count derived from the difference between a computed address and a fixed base. It then stores a four-byte marker value in a global variable.

name: loop_table_entry_until_clear
description: Looks up a longword in a table indexed by the input scaled by four and branches on its sign. While a status bit stays set it repeatedly calls a routine, then returns zero; the decompiled loop is partly unreliable.

name: compute_bounds_into_list_entry
description: Adds record position and size fields to produce corner values, then writes a 16-bit address and derived flag bits into an entry of a list when the list pointer is set. The listing is cut off, so the remaining steps are not described.

name: initialize_interrupt_vectors_and_hardware
description: Saves six longwords from a low-memory vector region into a global buffer and copies several custom-chip register values into it. It writes a clear-all value to the interrupt request register and installs handler addresses into a run of low-memory vector slots.

name: initialize_list_head_entries
description: Writes two words and a sentinel longword into a global buffer, then stores the buffer's address in the record and in a second pointer. It clears one word in the record and sets another control word.

name: mask_status_and_set_limit
description: Writes a masked copy of one record word into a second record word, then sets a 16-bit limit field to 4095.

name: mask_status_and_set_limit
description: Writes a masked copy of one record word into a second record word, then sets a 16-bit limit field to 4095.

name: mask_status_and_set_limit
description: Writes a masked copy of one record word into a second record word, then sets a 16-bit limit field to 4095.

name: repeat_call_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls a routine and checks its return value, looping until that value is zero. The call goes through a jump-table entry that passes control to a fixed address elsewhere in memory.

name: return_masked_status_bits
description: Returns the status bits selected by a fixed mask from a byte in the record, namely the second and fifth bits.

name: poll_until_zero_flag
description: Repeatedly calls a routine, looping until the processor's zero condition is set. The loop has no other work.

name: wait_while_status_bit_set
description: Loops while bit one of a status byte in the record is set, then returns. It makes no calls.

name: find_containing_list_entry
description: Scans a list of eight-word entries for the first one whose four bounds enclose the record's two coordinate values. It records the matching index and returns a coordinate difference, or -1 when no entry matches or the list ends.

name: copy_masked_flags_with_limit
description: Copies a masked value from one record word into a second word using a fixed bit mask. When the masked result is nonzero it also sets a 16-bit limit field to 4095.

name: poll_cia_bit_and_dispatch
description: Reads a bit in a CIA register and, when it is set, waits briefly and clears a bit in a second CIA port. It then either calls a routine or toggles and stores a table entry, depending on a status flag. The CIA-A port it touches carries fire-button and disk status.

name: forward_routine_result_stack
description: Calls a routine, then returns the stack argument it was given unchanged.

name: store_translated_input_byte
description: Sets a status flag and stores the input byte in the record, translating it through a lookup table that is offset by a fixed amount when a second flag is set. It then sets another status bit and calls routines. The decompiled listing contains bad-instruction warnings, so the remainder is unreliable.

name: append_character_to_ring_buffer
description: Writes an input character into a 32-entry buffer at a running index, then advances the index and wraps it to the start after the last entry. A carriage-return code sets a status flag, is stored as an asterisk, and restarts the index.

name: copy_text_with_control_codes
description: Copies a null-terminated text string into a buffer, passing control characters and high-bit codes to routines and storing printable characters directly. It ends the copied text with an asterisk. The referenced text reads as a disk-insert prompt.

name: format_signed_number_text
description: Converts a number into characters, writing an optional minus sign first and then digits from repeated calls. The listing is partial, so the exact digit handling is not fully recovered.

name: copy_text_until_asterisk
description: Calls a routine to set up a source, then copies characters from it into the destination until an asterisk is reached. It finishes with a space character.

name: copy_counted_text_with_terminator
description: Copies characters from a source into a destination for up to a given count, stopping early after an asterisk is copied. It ends the destination with an asterisk.

name: skip_asterisk_terminated_strings
description: Finds the start of an asterisk-terminated string in a table using the low five bits of an input, then skips forward past as many strings as a second input gives.

name: clear_pending_value_and_advance
description: Calls a routine, clears a longword field if it is nonzero, then calls a second routine. It stores the sum of two record words into a field and copies a third word, and the facts reference a disk-insert prompt string.

name: compose_text_with_four_calls
description: The 113-instruction routine is partly described by its listing: it makes four unnamed calls and is reached through an address-taken reference, called by two routines. The listing is cut off, so its exact steps are not described.

name: clear_byte_grid_rows
description: Calls one routine, then zeroes a rectangular block of bytes in a buffer. The row count comes from a record word plus an input, and each row's width and stride come from input values.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing any work. The facts report 19 instructions, which does not match the empty body shown, so the listing may be incomplete.

name: check_vowel_characters
description: Calls routines and returns a value, with a referenced character list of vowels in upper and lower case. The listing shows only a single call and a return, so the exact check is not recovered.

name: sum_table_values_until_match
description: Walks bytes from a pointer until one equals the input byte. For each byte before the match it adds one plus a value looked up in a global table, and returns the total.

name: write_five_digit_decimal
description: Writes the absolute value of an input number into five consecutive text bytes as ASCII digits, most significant digit first.

name: write_five_digit_decimal
description: Writes the absolute value of an input number into five consecutive text bytes as ASCII digits, most significant digit first.

name: write_five_digit_decimal
description: Writes the absolute value of an input number into five consecutive text bytes as ASCII digits, most significant digit first.

name: write_five_digit_decimal
description: Writes the absolute value of an input number into five consecutive text bytes as ASCII digits, most significant digit first.

name: parse_decimal_digit_string
description: Converts a string of decimal digit characters into a number by multiplying each digit by a weight from a table and summing the results. It also sets a flag bit in a record word.

name: handle_masked_input_flags
description: Copies a masked form of an input word into a second record word. When one flag bit is set it stores a value, calls a routine and clears a bit in a status byte, and other branches handle the remaining masked bits.

name: dispatch_status_bit_handlers
description: Checks bit seven of one status byte and, when it is set, calls a handler through a pointer table. Otherwise it checks bit seven of a second status byte and calls a second handler through the same kind of table. The decompiler could not recover the table targets.

name: advance_and_compare_counter
description: When one status bit is set, it increments a 16-bit counter in the record and a second counter, then compares the first against a value looked up through a pointer and table. It calls routines according to the result, and part of the listing is not recovered.

name: update_cia_derived_state
description: Computes a derived byte from a global value and a record byte, stores it in a record field, and updates a pair of record bytes through a difference calculation. It touches CIA hardware registers and calls two routines; the listing is cut short, so later steps are not described.

name: decode_byte_pairs_until_flagged
description: Reads byte pairs from a stream pointer held in the record, decrementing a repeat count in the first byte and advancing when it reaches zero. While the second byte's high bit is clear it calls two routines; once set it stores the byte in the record and finishes with a short delay loop.

name: busy_delay_loop
description: Counts an input value down to minus one as a short busy-wait, then returns.

name: clear_status_bit_one
description: Clears bit one of a status byte in the record and returns.

name: initialize_status_and_fields
description: Waits until bit one of a status byte is clear, then sets it. It stores a callback pointer, copies a longword from the input record, clears several record words, and sets a limit word to 426.

name: initialize_alternate_fields
description: Waits until bit one of a status byte is clear, then sets it. It stores a callback pointer and a longword from the input record, clears several record words, and sets a limit word to 938.

name: zero_words_and_trailing_byte
description: Zeroes consecutive 16-bit words for half of an input length, then zeroes one trailing byte when the input length is odd.

name: store_fixed_longword_value
description: Stores a fixed 32-bit value at the address held in an address register and returns.

name: call_four_routines_in_loop
description: Calls four routines in sequence inside a loop whose continuation depends on an incoming condition flag. The listing shows the loop exit only through that flag.

name: set_flag_and_check_result
description: Sets bit zero of a status byte, stores a fixed 32-bit value into a global, and calls two routines. It returns zero after clearing bit five when a local flag stays clear, and minus one otherwise.

name: compare_longword_blocks
description: Compares two blocks of longwords element by element for a count given by an input. It returns minus one at the first mismatch and zero when every element matches.

name: load_table_entry_into_record
description: Stores an address and an index in the record, then reads a table row selected by the index and scaled by 32. It stores a word from the row as a longword and a byte from it into record fields, and returns a word from the row.

name: write_marker_and_poll_loop
description: Writes a four-byte marker value to a fixed memory location, then loops making calls and clearing a request flag in a record byte. The listing is partial, so later branches are not fully described.

name: poll_table_flag_loop
description: Checks the sign of a table word selected by an input. When a status bit is set it loops calling routines while the sign condition holds, then returns zero.

name: poll_table_flag_loop
description: Checks the sign of a table word selected by an input. When a status bit is set it loops calling routines while the sign condition holds, then returns zero.

name: combine_two_small_routine_results
description: Calls two small routines that return zero and 255, then writes their results into a buffer. The decompiled listing contains unreachable blocks, so only the call structure is described.

name: process_flagged_record_state
description: Calls four routines and uses a record byte's flag state to choose one of two paths, setting that byte to 255 along the way. The decompiled listing is partial, so the remaining branches are not described.

name: store_parameters_and_select_mode
description: Stores an input byte and two input words into record fields, then picks one of two mode values from a flag bit and stores it. It makes four calls, and the rest of the listing is not fully recovered.

name: write_cia_port_sequence
description: Writes six byte values to one CIA location, clearing one bit at a time from bit six down to bit three and then restoring all bits. The 60-instruction count suggests more code than the listing shows.

name: call_three_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls three routines one after another and returns. It has no other work of its own.

name: wait_port_bit_with_timeout
description: Polls a bit in a CIA-A port value and returns as soon as that bit is clear. It gives up after a fixed countdown of sixteen thousand iterations.

name: set_cia_b_port_mask
description: Chooses one of two bit masks depending on a record flag, stores the mask in the record, and writes its inverse, limited to seven bits, to a CIA-B port register.

name: toggle_counter_and_flag
description: Steps a global counter down by two and wraps it to eighteen when it goes negative. It toggles bit four of a record word, touches CIA port registers, and calls two routines.

name: loop_calls_on_condition
description: Calls routines in a loop whose continuation depends on an incoming condition flag, with an inner endless loop once the flag is set. The listing does not show the callees' details.

name: wait_port_bit_then_clear
description: Repeatedly calls a routine while bit four of a CIA-A port value stays set, then zeroes a record word.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: If a record word is negative it calls a routine. It then computes the difference between two record words and, when that difference is nonzero, adds it to the second word and makes calls once per unit of the difference.

name: repeat_call_pairs_by_count
description: Makes one call, then loops a number of times taken from a register, making two calls on each pass.

name: busy_wait_fixed_count
description: Counts down from a fixed value of 4616 as a busy-wait, then returns.

name: write_two_bytes_to_port
description: Writes two byte values in sequence to the same memory location, so the second value overwrites the first.

name: no_op_return_routine
description: Returns immediately with no work. The listing shows only a return, although the facts report 17 instructions, so the body may be incomplete.

name: initialize_timing_record
description: Stores an input word and a set of fixed 16-bit constants into a record, stores two callback pointers, and copies a longword from a global variable.

name: configure_record_from_parameters
description: Writes a series of fixed values into a record, including a flag word and a longword copied from another record. It also stores a value one greater than a field with its top bit set. The same word is written twice, so the second value stands.

name: wait_flag_bit_with_timeout
description: Calls a routine, then polls a flag word while keeping only bit one of it, giving up after a countdown of sixteen thousand passes. It then stores sixteen thousand in another record word.

name: halt_in_endless_loop
description: Enters an endless loop and never returns. The facts show it touches a CIA-B interrupt control register.

name: start_channel_and_wait_flag
description: Writes a fixed set of control values into a record, where the second write to the same word overrides the first. It copies a longword from a second record, calls a routine, and polls a flag word until bit one is set, within a fixed countdown.

name: copy_list_entries_with_bounds
description: Walks a list of short values in nested loops, copying each value from a source to a destination within a bounds check. The listing shows the copy loops but not all of the bounds handling.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one as its result, without other work.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. The facts show it is referenced as a callback and called once.

name: copy_longs_within_bounds
description: Copies up to 128 longwords into a destination region offset from a base address, stopping early when the destination passes a bounds limit. It returns zero on completion and minus one when its initial check fails.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one and nothing else.

name: busy_delay_from_input
description: Counts down from an input value as a short busy-wait, then returns.

name: fill_alternating_pattern_block
description: Fills a block of longwords with an alternating bit pattern, adds one word of the same pattern at the end, and then writes another repeated longword pattern in a loop that makes calls on each pass. The listing is partial, and the purpose of the patterns is not determined from the facts.

name: compute_bit_mix_and_store
description: Calls a routine, combines its result with an input value through shifts and bitwise operations, then masks the sign bit when a flag byte is set. It stores the result and updates a status bit in the following record byte; further branches are not fully shown.

name: store_bit_mix_and_flag
description: Combines an input with a second value through shifts and bitwise operations, masks the sign bit when a flag byte is set, and stores the result. It then sets or clears bit seven of the byte that follows the stored longword and makes one call.

name: store_seven_bit_value
description: Stores the input byte with its top bit cleared at the address held in an address register, then returns.

name: poll_until_zero_twice
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until a value it reports becomes zero, then does the same for a second value, and returns the two saved register values unchanged.

name: build_crc16_lookup_table
description: Builds a 256-entry lookup table of 16-bit checksum values by shifting each entry through eight bits with a 16-bit CRC polynomial. It stores each entry's high and low bytes into two parallel tables.

name: copy_block_then_decode_tokens
description: Copies an initial block of bytes from a source table into a buffer, then runs a token-driven decoding loop. The loop branches on small token values and advances its pointers by fixed amounts, and it writes to the 16-colour palette register. The decompiled listing contains bad-instruction warnings, so the exact token meanings are partly unrecovered.

name: extract_shifted_bit_value
description: Reads a longword from the address register at a small negative offset and writes its low byte into the low half of a destination word. It returns the longword shifted right by one place with the top bit forced on.

name: shift_register_bits_with_refill
description: Shifts a data register right one bit per pass for a count taken from another register. It calls a routine to refill the register whenever it becomes zero, and the loop runs once per count.

name: set_global_and_trap
description: Stores the address of the current routine into a global variable, then executes a trap instruction with operand zero. The trap's effect is outside the listing.

name: wait_for_port_bit_sequence
description: Polls bit six of a CIA-A port value, calling routines between polls, and returns once the port's bit sequence has been waited on. It makes four calls in total.

name: initialize_copper_and_interrupts
description: Disables DMA, interrupt enable and interrupt request bits with a clear-all value, then sets a control word from a custom-chip register. It fills table entries from a second table, and the facts show writes to the copper list location and jump registers.

name: restore_saved_hardware_words
description: Disables DMA and interrupt bits with a clear-all value, then writes two saved control words back to those registers. It copies a pointer from a table entry into the record and stores an input word.

name: read_status_byte_increment_counter
description: Reads a status byte from the record. When that byte equals minus one it adds a fixed step of 273 to a global counter, waits until the byte reads zero, and returns zero; otherwise it returns the byte.

name: read_status_byte_decrement_counter
description: Reads a status byte from the record. When that byte equals minus one it subtracts a fixed step of 273 from a global counter, waits until the byte reads zero, and returns zero; otherwise it returns the byte.

name: clear_large_buffer_bytes
description: Zeroes a block of 15360 bytes in a fixed buffer, one byte per pass.

name: decode_run_table_into_rows
description: Walks a byte stream from a global buffer, treating zero bytes as row breaks that advance an output pointer by 640 bytes. Other bytes are copied into the output with a running column count. The listing is partial.

name: clear_word_block
description: Zeroes a block of 2854 words starting at a fixed buffer address.

name: reset_global_and_run_steps
description: Clears a global variable and makes seven calls to unnamed routines in sequence, then returns zero. The facts note a custom-chip register access.

name: copy_entry_fields_to_buffer
description: Walks a null-terminated table of record pointers. For each entry it copies one byte from each of twelve records spaced 36 bytes apart into a global buffer, then moves to the next table entry.

name: forbid_and_configure_hardware
description: Makes a system library call, then stores interrupt and DMA words from the record with the top bit forced on. It writes a clear-all value to the DMA and interrupt registers and sets a 32 value in a record field, then makes several calls. The listing is partial.

name: fill_accumulating_longwords
description: Writes a running longword value into a table, storing its high and low words at a stride of eight bytes. Each pass adds a step to the running value, for a count set by the caller.

name: open_and_close_graphics_library
description: Opens a system library by name through Exec calls, copies a longword from the returned library into the record, then closes the library. The referenced text is the library name.

name: scale_table_pairs_by_four
description: Multiplies both words of each of forty-four pairs in a fixed table by four.

name: build_shifted_row_masks
description: Fills sixteen rows of eight longwords with values taken from a global block. Each value is combined by OR with the row index shifted into high and low bit positions.

name: build_reciprocal_table
description: Builds a table of 16-bit reciprocals by dividing a fixed large constant by each even divisor from 256 up to just under 8192 and storing the quotient.

name: run_frame_loop_with_calls
description: Runs an endless loop that waits until a masked timer value matches a fixed value, then makes nine calls and one indirect call through a table. Each pass repeats the same sequence.

name: advance_step_counter_with_wrap
description: If a global flag is zero, it waits for a status bit to clear and returns zero. Otherwise it calls a routine and increments a step counter; when the counter reaches thirteen it advances a table pointer and flag and resets the counter. It returns the counter.

name: render_text_glyph_columns
description: Looks up each character in a font table, indexed by its offset from the first printable character, and copies its eight column bytes into a bitmap buffer. Successive columns are written at a stride of forty bytes, repeating for every character.

name: update_counters_from_port_state
description: Reads record values and a CIA-A port bit to update counter and state fields, using arithmetic and bitwise steps. The referenced text reads as a short label string. The 153-instruction routine is only partly shown, so its full behaviour is not described.

name: copy_row_blocks_between_buffers
description: Copies blocks of rows between two buffers, moving longwords in groups for each row. Row offsets of forty bytes are computed from an index and its complement. The listing is cut off partway through the copy steps.

name: clear_mirrored_table_rows
description: Zeroes ten longwords in each of two table rows, one selected by an index and the other by its mirror from the far end. It then updates the index for the next pass.

name: advance_double_buffer_offsets
description: When a countdown reaches zero it resets it to six, advances a masked offset forward and a second offset backward by two, and copies table words selected by those offsets into output locations. Further copies depend on the offset range, and the listing is cut off.

name: scan_leading_text_marker
description: When a countdown reaches zero it resets it to six, then reads a string pointer and skips leading characters that match a marker letter, setting a fixed value for each one. The listing is partial, so the remaining steps are not described.

name: combine_indexed_table_values
description: Writes a 16-bit control value to a custom-chip register, then reads several table entries through index offsets and combines them with arithmetic before calling a routine. The listing is partial, so the final outputs are not fully described.

name: copy_byte_load_table_words
description: Writes a byte at an offset from the record pointer and loads several table words into local variables for later steps. The rest of the routine is not shown in the listing.

name: copy_table_pairs_with_index
description: Walks forty-four table pairs, reading each pair and writing computed values into an output table. A custom-chip register is touched, and the listing stops before the arithmetic is shown in full.

name: wait_then_update_table_outputs
description: Waits until bit six of a status byte in the record is clear, then updates several output words from table lookups and bit operations, making three calls. The listing is partial.

name: update_bit_and_compare_values
description: Sets a bit in a memory byte selected by a bit index, computes a value with bit six set, and compares it against a limit before returning. The listing is short and only partly recovered.

name: interpolate_coordinate_between_bounds
description: Compares a coordinate against a bound, then computes an interpolated value from two endpoint differences using division. It returns early in several cases and calls two routines.

name: interpolate_span_endpoints
description: Handles several sign and bound cases for two endpoints, computing an interpolated coordinate by division and writing the results with one call. The 118-instruction routine is only partly shown, so its complete branch structure is not described.

name: initialize_record_after_wait
description: Writes a control word with the set bit and one enable bit, waits for a status bit to clear, then sets several record fields to constants, including all-ones and small limit values. The listing is partial.

name: initialize_timer_record_fields
description: Waits until a status bit is clear, then sets several record fields to constants and to a value computed from a global. It includes a 16-bit timer value of 10004.

name: set_timer_record_from_global
description: Waits until a status bit is clear, then sets a record longword to a fixed constant, clears a word, copies a global longword into the record, and sets a timer word to 10004.

name: swap_globals_and_store_halves
description: Swaps two global longwords, then stores the low and high words of the earlier value into two fixed memory words.

name: remap_keyboard_serial_code
description: Adjusts a keyboard character code through a long chain of comparisons that add or subtract ten to selected values. The facts show it touches the keyboard serial register.
